questions.text: $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\cos (\sin x)-\cos x}{x^{4}}$ is equal to :

options.D:
$\frac{1}{12}$

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)
Sol. $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\cos (\sin x)-\cos x}{x^{4}} ;\left(\frac{0}{0}\right)$
$$\begin{array}{c}
\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{2 \cdot \sin \left(\frac{x+\sin x}{2}\right) \cdot \sin \left(\frac{x-\sin x}{2}\right)}{x^{4}}\right) \\
\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} 2\left(\frac{\sin \left(\frac{x+\sin x}{2}\right)}{\left(\frac{x+\sin x}{2}\right)}\right)\left(\frac{\sin \left(\frac{x-\sin x}{2}\right)}{\left(\frac{x-\sin x}{2}\right)}\right) \frac{\left(\frac{x+\sin x}{2}\right)}{x^{4}}\left(\frac{x-\sin x}{2}\right) \\
\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{x^{2}-\sin ^{2} x}{2 x^{4}}\right):\left(\frac{0}{0}\right)
\end{array}$$

Apply L-Hopital Rule :
$$\begin{array}{l}

\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{2 x-\sin 2 x}{8 x^{3}} ; \frac{0}{0}: \text { Again apply L-Hopital rule } \\

\end{array}$$

questions.text: Consider a cuboid of sides 2x, 4x and 5x and a closed hemisphere of radius r . If the sum of their surface areas is a constant k , then the ratio $\mathrm{x}: \mathrm{r}$, for which the sum of their volumes is maximum, is :

options.D:
19 : 15

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
Sol. Surface area $=76 \mathrm{x}^{2}+3 \pi \mathrm{r}^{2}=$ constant (K)
$$\begin{array}{l}
V=40 x^{3}+\frac{2}{3} \pi r^{3} \\
{\left[76 x^{2}+3 \pi r^{2}=K\right]} \\
r^{2}=\frac{K-76 x^{2}}{3 \pi} \\
r=\left(\frac{K-76 x^{2}}{3 \pi}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \\
V=40 x^{3}+\frac{2}{3} \pi\left(\frac{K-76 x^{2}}{3 \pi}\right)^{\frac{3}{2}} \\
\frac{d V}{d x}=120 x^{2}+\frac{2}{3} \pi \cdot \frac{3}{2}\left(\frac{K-76 x^{2}}{3 \pi}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \cdot\left(\frac{-76(2 x)}{3 \pi}\right)
\end{array}$$

Put
$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{\mathrm{dV}}{\mathrm{dx}} & =0 \Rightarrow 120 x^{2}+\frac{2}{3} \pi \cdot \frac{3}{2}\left(\frac{\mathrm{~K}-76 x^{2}}{3 \pi}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \cdot\left(\frac{-76(2 \mathrm{x})}{3 \pi}\right)=0 \\
& \Rightarrow 120 \mathrm{x}^{2}=\frac{152 \mathrm{x}}{3}\left(\frac{\mathrm{k}-76 \mathrm{x}^{2}}{3 \pi}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{45}{19} x^{2}=\mathrm{x}\left(\frac{\mathrm{k}-76 x^{2}}{3 \pi}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} ; \mathrm{x} \neq 0 \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{45}{19} \mathrm{x}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{k}-76 x^{2}}{3 \pi}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \Rightarrow\left(\frac{45}{19}\right)^{2} x^{2}=\frac{\mathrm{k}-76 x^{2}}{3 \pi} \\
& \Rightarrow\left(\frac{45}{19}\right)^{2} x^{2}=\mathrm{r}^{2} \Rightarrow \frac{x^{2}}{\mathrm{r}^{2}}=\left(\frac{19}{45}\right)^{2} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{r}}=\frac{19}{45}
\end{aligned}$$
